- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative, model overreacts to sentiment shift — dampen forecast slope by 15–25% in the following 5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.5) over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate future prices — reduce forecast by 2–4% per day of sustained positive sentiment.
- Model often lags in recognizing sentiment-driven reversals — if sentiment turns negative after 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
